body: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances language models with external knowledge, but the lengthy retrieved context inflates the input and degrades inference efficiency. Soft context compression encodes each document into a substantially shorter embedding sequence. However, most existing approaches are trained by distilling outputs from uncompressed RAG systems, inherently limiting their performance relative to the original model. To address this limitation, we propose DEX-Comp, a two-stage training recipe: Pure Distillation warm-starts the compression model on the uncompressed RAG's correct responses only, and Hard Exploration then runs reinforcement learning solely on queries the uncompressed RAG fails, forcing the model to explore computation patterns better suited to compressed representations. On five open-domain QA benchmarks at retrieval depths from top-5 to top-30, DEX-Comp compresses retrieved contexts by 16× and accelerates inference by 4×--24×, while achieving performance comparable to or exceeding the uncompressed RAG baseline across retrieval depths. Ablations and evaluations across diverse datasets and backbones further confirm the contribution of each stage and the generalization of our approach.
summaryZh: 针对RAG系统中长检索上下文引发的推理效率低下问题，本文提出了一种名为DEX-Comp的两阶段软上下文压缩训练方案。该方案首先通过纯蒸馏热启动压缩模型，接着利用强化学习专门针对未压缩RAG失败的查询进行硬探索。在多个公开问答基准测试中，DEX-Comp在将检索上下文压缩16倍的同时，加速推理4倍到24倍，并保持了与未压缩基线相当或更高的性能。
